context_needed: BRAC's Targeting the Ultra Poor (TUP/CFPR) programme in Bangladesh, household panel 2002-2011 (2,098 treatment and 1,940 control households, Table A3 notes, same page). The impact estimates are in Tables 1-5 (DD and DD-PSM, pp. 7-11). Section III (p. 6) says the PSM first step is 'a probit model using baseline (2002) data' and points to Table A4 for it. The dependent variable is programme participation, so every coefficient describes who joined, not what the programme did.

rule: A probit or logit of who joins the programme (the first step of propensity-score matching) has covariates as rows and no programme term: nothing in it is stored, even rows named like outcomes such as livestock owned, because they are baseline predictors of selection.
